clue.text: Production of DNA units is to follow

indicators.note: 'is to follow' places the small word after the DNA units

parts.note: genes are the units of heredity carried on DNA
taken as written

explanation.surface: A biology note about how DNA's coding segments come to be produced.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis is the origin or coming into being of something, its creation.

clue.text: Delightful slovenly woman is a talkative person

parts.note: something great fun is informally 'a gas'
bag is a derogatory slang term for an unkempt woman

explanation.surface: A charming but untidy woman turns out to be a chatterbox.
explanation.definitionFit: A windbag who talks endlessly is informally given this name.

clue.text: Country to progress rapidly, so to speak

indicators.note: the phrase signals that the words are judged by their spoken sound

parts.note: to 'nip on' is to move ahead quickly

explanation.surface: A remark about a nation that is advancing fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippon is the native Japanese name for Japan.

clue.text: Fishmonger perhaps who has no partners

explanation.surface: A fish seller who works entirely alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of flatfish deals in sole; in business, a self-employed person with no partners is so called.

clue.text: Prepared to fight

parts.note: set means ready or prepared
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone ready to start a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief but vigorous argument or brawl.

clue.text: Mother repeatedly put cap in the middle for a holy leader

indicators.note: the headwear is placed between the two halves
the word for mother is used twice over, one after another

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a cap is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: Mum keeps placing a hat in the centre to honour a revered guru.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' gives MAMA; 'in the middle' puts HAT between the two MAs.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma, 'great soul', is a title given to a revered sage, famously Gandhi.

clue.text: One million cycles per second could graze them badly

indicators.note: grazing done badly suggests the letters are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that livestock might graze people roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit of frequency equal to a million hertz, each hertz being one cycle a second.

clue.text: Knocks the best-sellers

explanation.surface: A note about chart-toppers taking a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Blows or strikes are this, and so are popular records or successes.

clue.text: Poet sent on, travelling round New York

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the state abbreviation
letters that are travelling are on the move, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet is dispatched on a journey around New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' turns SENT ON into TENSON; 'round' puts it around NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Tennyson was Queen Victoria's Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Stranger learned, by end of May, about the island

indicators.note: read as 'more strange', it tells us the letters are made odd by rearranging
the final letter of the month is taken

explanation.surface: A newcomer studied the island near the end of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' turns LEARNED into ALDERNE; 'end of' gives Y from May. Alderney is one of the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Alderney is one of the Channel Islands, a British Crown dependency off France.

clue.text: Part of flower leaps out

indicators.note: out suggests letters thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something in a flower suddenly springs out.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepal is one of the leaf-like outer parts that enclose a bud.

clue.text: Drunk with sweetheart in the end adjusted his belt perhaps

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk

indicators.note: the heart letter sits inside the word for finish

parts.note: end is a finish
the heart of 'sweet' is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: A tipsy man with his lover finally hitches up his belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is read as the heart of 'sweet', the letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: Belts and other straps are made tighter, pulled in more closely.

clue.text: Sign of omission

parts.note: a punctuation mark that stands where letters have been left out, as in can't

explanation.definitionFit: The raised comma marks dropped letters in contractions such as don't.

clue.text: Colourful worker?

parts.note: not a lively personality but someone whose job is to add colour to cloth

explanation.definitionFit: A tradesperson who colours fabrics with stains and pigments.

clue.text: Found underground? It depends

explanation.surface: Something in a cave with an uncertain answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cave formation of limestone grows in caverns, and it hangs from the roof, an old sense of 'depend'.

clue.text: Beat teacher first in well-timed act

indicators.note: the teacher word is placed ahead of the beat word

parts.note: a schoolmaster is a teacher
a stroke is a beat, as of a clock or oar

explanation.surface: A teacher strikes first with perfect timing.
explanation.definitionFit: A brilliantly judged move or coup, done at exactly the right moment.

clue.text: Not one who only moves in time to the Water Music

definitions.text: Not one who only moves in time to the Water Music

parts.words: Not one who only moves in time to the Water Music
parts.note: reads as about Handel's suite, but a 'water' performer would be one who uses a tap, here the shoe-tapping kind

explanation.surface: A dancer who does more than sway to Handel's Water Music.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer whose metal-plated shoes beat out rhythms on the floor.

clue.text: I am one on board worthy of being copied

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
I is the Roman numeral one
a table is a board, as in 'bed and board'

explanation.surface: Someone joining a board feels they are a fine example to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Something capable of imitation can be copied or reproduced.

clue.text: When he has a meal, the working population is reduced

definitions.text: When he has a meal, the working population is reduced

parts.words: When he has a meal, the working population is reduced
parts.note: sounds like economics, but the workers are worker insects, eaten by this creature

explanation.definitionFit: A long-snouted mammal that feeds on colonies of insects, termites and workers alike.

clue.text: Found in an arboretum perhaps but it is not to scale

definitions.text: Found in an arboretum perhaps but it is not to scale

parts.words: Found in an arboretum perhaps but it is not to scale
parts.note: not a model out of proportion but a spiky conifer said to defeat climbing primates

explanation.definitionFit: The Chilean pine, whose sharp scaly branches are said to baffle even an ape.

clue.text: African country, one under petticoat government?

indicators.note: in a down answer the numeral sits below the government phrase

parts.note: rule by women, read here as 'ma law', mother's law
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A nation where the women rule the roost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Petticoat government' means rule by women at home, read as MA LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked nation in south-east Africa.

clue.text: It is hard to find fish in a dirty place

indicators.note: the fish is placed inside the dirty place

parts.note: a sty, a pigsty, is a filthy place
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: It is difficult to catch fish in a filthy spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely means hard and unyielding, like steel.

clue.text: See 18
Skilled work, it sounds a convenient trade

indicators.note: it sounds tells us to judge the phrase by its pronunciation

parts.note: handy means convenient and a craft is a trade

explanation.surface: Manual skill seems to be a useful occupation.
explanation.definitionFit: Craftwork made by hand, such as pottery or weaving.

clue.text: Mouth of the Dee?

parts.note: reads as the Welsh river's estuary, but Dee is also the letter D, whose code word this is

explanation.definitionFit: A delta is a river mouth, and in the phonetic alphabet it stands for the letter D.

clue.text: One not expressing approval in the meantime

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of letters of the last words

explanation.surface: Someone who withholds approval for now.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent of something, one who is against it.

clue.text: Scientific gardens?

parts.note: the adjective for plant science, which describes famous gardens like Kew

explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the study of plants, as in gardens kept for research.

clue.text: I reckon to be angry

parts.note: taken as written
to rate is to reckon or estimate

explanation.surface: Someone thinks they are cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means furious or very cross.

clue.text: Nobleman, one with the Queen before now

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
I is the Roman numeral one
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A peer has an audience with the monarch ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means at a previous time, sooner.

clue.text: Pleasing feature that could be arranged anytime

indicators.note: the letters may be put into a new order

explanation.surface: A nice extra that can be set up whenever you like.
explanation.definitionFit: An amenity is a pleasant or useful facility, such as a pool at a hotel.
